device.description: 8-bit 100 us microprocessor-compatible SAR ADC with differential input, on-chip clock and 3-state data bus
device.note: adc0804-n.pdf (SNOSBI1C) p.3 pin functions, p.4 recommended operating conditions, p.5-6 AC characteristics (conversion time, tACC, t1H/t0H, logic input levels), p.7 Figures 1-2 (start conversion, output enable and INTR reset), p.11 detailed description (start, INTR), p.14 digital control inputs, p.28 restart / continuous conversions

commands.name: Start conversion (CS and WR low, starts on release)

pages: p.3 (pins), p.4 (ROC: VCC 4.5-5.5 V), p.5 (TC 103-114 us at fCLK 640 kHz, 66-73 clocks), p.6 (tACC 135/200 ns, t1H/t0H 125/200 ns, tWI/tRI 300/450 ns, VIN(1) up to 15 V), p.7 (Figures 1-2), p.11 (start F/F, INTR), p.14 (CS/RD/WR active low), p.28 (restart, free-running)
notModeled: analog input, VREF/2 span adjustment and the differential VIN(-) offset (the result is always the 0 V code 0x00)
the conversion is clocked by CLK IN / the CLK R RC oscillator (64 clocks + up to 8 clocks of start latency); the model uses the fixed 114 us maximum at fCLK = 640 kHz
CLK IN Schmitt trigger and CLK R RC oscillator output (CLK R is never driven)
a new start (CS and WR low) also resets INTR; ready clears only on a read of the result
the converter is held in reset while CS and WR stay low (the model starts at WR/CS release, which matches)
restart during a conversion leaves the previous result in the output latch
free-running mode with INTR tied to WR and the power-up initialising WR pulse
INTR delay from WR/RD falling (tWI/tRI 450 ns max), and the 8-clock INTR SET pulse when CS and RD are held low
pin names: DB0 (LSB) is named DB0, VCC (or VREF) is named VCC (its use as the upper ladder reference is analog), VIN(–) is written VIN(-)
variants: ADC0801/0803/0805 share the datasheet (PDIP only, not in the skeleton); ADC0804 (separate spec) is the same digital design, differing in accuracy (+-1 LSB unadjusted) and VREF/2 input resistance (1.1 kOhm vs 8 kOhm)
